# What Actually Moves Catch Rates (and What Doesn't)

> Ranked by strength of evidence. The Catch Log app's "best times" score weights these accordingly:
> saltwater = tide movement 55% · dawn/dusk light 45%; freshwater = dawn/dusk light only. Solunar periods are not used.

| Factor | Evidence | What it is | How to use it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Water temperature** | Strong evidence | Fish are cold-blooded: metabolism, feeding and location all track water temp. A 5°F change matters more than any moon table. | The app shows the live reading from the nearest NOAA/USGS sensor (check it from home before a trip), the normal for the date, and whether each fish is in its prime range. Log the real number on the trip with a $10 thermometer. In fall, the first cool fronts that drop water into the 60s°F turn on trout, reds and bass. |
| **Moving water (tide current)** | Strong evidence | Current moves bait; predators set up where current delivers it (points, creek mouths, jetty tips, pier pilings). Slack water is usually the slowest bite. | The app's tide factor scores mid-tide (fastest flow) highest, and the Times screen flags big-tide days from NOAA data (bigger range = faster current). Plan to be fishing during the middle 2–4 hours of a rising or falling tide. Inside creeks/the MarshWalk, the last half of the falling tide pulls bait out of the marsh. |
| **Low light (dawn & dusk)** | Moderate evidence | Many predators (bass, trout, reds, bluefish) feed hardest in low light, when they have the visual edge over bait. | Be lines-in at sunrise. When a moving tide lines up with dawn or dusk, that's the best window of the day. |
| **Finding bait** | Strong evidence | No bait, no fish. Diving birds, nervous water, and mullet schools along the beach are where the bite is. | In October, follow the mullet run: blues, reds and flounder sit right under the schools. |
| **Weather fronts / barometric pressure** | Mixed evidence | Fishing often improves ahead of a front and slows for 1–2 days after a hard cold front (bluebird skies). Controlled studies on pressure itself are inconsistent. | SCDNR notes cold fronts trigger the fall trout bite. Fish the day before a front; slow down and fish deeper right after. |
| **Solunar majors/minors & moon phase** | Weak evidence | Popular since 1926 but poorly supported: a 2023 peer-reviewed trout study found NO relationship between catch rate and solunar periods, moon phase, or illumination (air temp predicted better). Bass research (Univ. of Florida) found no new/full moon boost. Some reef fish show species-specific lunar effects. | NOT used in this app (removed Oct 2026). The moon's one real effect on inshore fishing is through TIDES: new/full moons make bigger tides and faster current. The Times screen shows that directly as "Big tides / Small tides vs average" from NOAA data. |
| **Circle hooks & quick releases** | Strong evidence | Circle hooks greatly reduce deep-hooking and post-release death for bait fishing (Cooke & Suski 2004 review). Air exposure and rough handling raise release mortality. | Circle hooks are now REQUIRED in SC for natural bait on 4/0+ hooks for saltwater gamefish. Don't "set" a circle hook, just reel tight. Wet hands, horizontal support for big fish, photo fast, back in the water. |
| **Your own logbook** | Strong evidence | Local patterns beat generic tables. Catch-per-hour by tide stage, light and spot, from YOUR trips, is the same method fisheries scientists use (CPUE). | Log every trip, even skunks (effort counts). After ~10 trips, Stats → Insights shows catch-per-hour by tide stage and light period. Trust that over any app's prediction, including this one. |
